merger_description:
Sonnel Hospitality Group (**Sonnel Hospitality**) proposes to acquire the Peakhurst Inn Hotel at 705 Forest Road, Peakhurst NSW 2210 (trading as **The Peakhurst**).

Sonnel Hospitality proposes to acquire the freehold going concern of The Peakhurst, comprising the land, hotel building, NSW Hotel Liquor Licence, business, goodwill, plant, equipment and stock. The acquisition is structured as two concurrent asset purchases: freehold/land by Meerlen Pty Limited as trustee of Vic on the Park Trust, and business by Nelmeer Ashfield Pty Ltd as trustee of Nelmeer Ashfield Trading Trust.

Sonnel Hospitality (formerly Nelson Meers Hotel Group) is a privately-owned, community-driven hospitality group that owns and operates 19 hotels/pubs in Sydney. Its venues offer on-premises sale of alcohol, takeaway packaged liquor, food, gaming, TAB/Keno and accommodation.

Sonnel Hospitality currently operates two hotels within 5 km of The Peakhurst: Hurstville Ritz Hotel (350 Forest Road, Hurstville NSW 2220) and Wiley Park Hotel (67 King Georges Road, Wiley Park NSW). Wiley Park Hotel has an on-site bottle shop.

The Peakhurst is a full-service community hotel located at 705 Forest Road, Peakhurst NSW 2210, in the Georges River local government area of metropolitan Sydney. It is owned and operated by entities associated with JDA Collective.

Both parties supply hotel/hospitality services including the sale of alcohol for on-premises consumption, takeaway/packaged liquor (via attached bottle shops), food and beverage, gaming (electronic gaming machines), TAB/Keno wagering, short-term accommodation, and function/entertainment services.

determination_table_content.details:
Sonnel Hospitality Group (Sonnel Hospitality) proposes to acquire
the freehold going concern of the Peakhurst Inn Hotel at 705 Forest
Road, Peakhurst NSW 2210 (trading as The Peakhurst), comprising
the land, hotel building, NSW Hotel Liquor Licence, business,
goodwill, plant, equipment and stock, as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).
The Acquisition is structured as two concurrent asset purchases:
freehold/land by Meerlen Pty Limited as trustee of Vic on the Park
Trust, and business by Nelmeer Ashfield Pty Ltd as trustee of
Nelmeer Ashfield Trading Trust.
Meerlen Pty Limited as trustee of Vic on the Park Trust applied for a
notification waiver in respect of the Acquisition.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Sonnel Hospitality (formerly Nelson Meers Hotel
Group), is a privately-owned, community-driven hospitality group that
owns and operates 19 hotels/pubs in Sydney. Its venues offer on-
premises sale of alcohol, takeaway packaged liquor, food, gaming,
TAB/Keno and accommodation.
The target, The Peakhurst, is a full-service community hotel located
at 705 Forest Road, Peakhurst NSW 2210, in the Georges River local
government area of metropolitan Sydney. It is owned and operated
by entities associated with JDA Collective.
Both parties supply hotel/hospitality services including the sale of
alcohol for on-premises consumption, takeaway/packaged liquor
(via attached bottle shops), food and beverage, gaming (electronic
gaming machines), TAB/Keno wagering, short-term accommodation,
and function/entertainment services.
Sonnel Hospitality currently operates two hotels within 5 km of The
Peakhurst: Hurstville Ritz Hotel (350 Forest Road, Hurstville NSW
2220) and Wiley Park Hotel (67 King Georges Road, Wiley Park
NSW). Wiley Park Hotel has an on-site bottle shop.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between Sonnel
Hospitality and The Peakhurst, based on number of
premises, in the supply of accommodation, dining, functions,
gaming and on-premises liquor services at pub-style venues
in the local area surrounding The Peakhurst
b. there are many alternative suppliers of accommodation,
dining, functions, gaming and on-premises liquor services in
the local area surrounding The Peakhurst.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
